title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the preceding pages): k is a field of characteristic ≠ 2 and J is a 4-element set. V_J = Ker(k^J → k, sum) is a 3-dimensional space and Σ is a conic in P(V_J). Grothendieck writes ω = ω_J for a 2-element set of 'racines circulaires' with ω' = −ω, i.e. a μ_2-torsor. For a μ_2-torsor ω and a vector space F, the twist F(ω) consists of symbols f∧ω subject to (−f)∧ω = f∧(−ω).

At a point t ∈ Σ, F_t ⊂ V_J is a line and t is the tangent line. One has O_t(1) ≅ Ḟ_t(ω) (Ḟ_t the dual line) and an isomorphism ν̌ : t^{⊗−2} ≅ F_t^{⊗2}(ω).

A 'Legendre pinning' (épinglage de Legendre) is a family κ_i : t ≅ O_t(1), indexed by i ∈ μ_4^* (the two primitive 4th roots of unity). It satisfies κ_{i'} = i κ_i for i' = 1/i, and condition (67): κ_i^{⊗2} = ν ∧ ω_i for some ω_i ∈ ω.

This page:
(68) Since κ_{i'}^{⊗2} = i^2 κ_i^{⊗2} = −κ_i^{⊗2}, one gets ω_{i'} = −ω_i. Hence i ↦ ω_i is a bijection α = α_κ : μ_4^* ≅ ω.

Margin note: once α is given, the two relations (67), one for each i, are equivalent. The next page confirms this.

Grothendieck then parametrizes κ, with α given in advance, through the contragredients κ̌_i. For δ ∈ t^* (nonzero vectors of t, with δ̌ the dual basis vector):
(69) κ̌_i(δ̌) = ψ^{ω_i}(δ) ∧ ω_i, with ψ^ω(δ) ∈ F_t.
(70) This gives a family (ψ^ω(δ))_{ω∈ω} ∈ F_t^ω.

Condition (66), κ̌_{i'} = (1/i) κ̌_i, becomes ψ^{ω'}∧ω' = (1/i) ψ^ω∧ω. Using ψ^{ω'}∧ω' = −ψ^{ω'}∧ω, this gives ψ^{ω'} = −(1/i) ψ^ω = i ψ^ω.
(71) ψ^{ω'}(δ) = i_ω ψ^ω(δ), where i_ω = α^{−1}(ω).
(72) Linearity in δ̌ (δ ↦ λδ sends δ̌ to λ^{−1}δ̌) gives ψ^ω(λδ) = λ^{−1} ψ^ω(δ).

The page ends announcing that (67) must still be expressed. On the next page this becomes (73) ψ^ω(δ)^{⊗2} = ν̌(δ̌^{⊗2}) ∧ ω. A lemma there identifies Legendre pinnings with systems (α, ψ) satisfying (71)–(73).

Purpose: an intrinsic, coordinate-free description of the rigidifications ('Legendre structures') on the conic/P^1 attached to a 4-point set. This underlies a canonical form for the Legendre family y² = x(x−1)(x−λ) in the study of moduli of elliptic curves with level-2 type structure over Z[1/2].
errors: No substantive error. The sign manipulations check out: ψ^{ω'}∧ω' = −ψ^{ω'}∧ω, and −1/i = i for i ∈ μ_4^*.
Consistency of (71) under applying it twice: i_{ω'} i_ω = (1/i)·i = 1, which holds.
The notation δ ∈ t^* must mean nonzero vectors of t, not the dual space. Otherwise (72) and the use of δ̌ do not make sense.

ideas.what: The bijection α_κ : μ_4^* ≅ ω induced by a Legendre pinning, between primitive 4th roots of unity and the μ_2-torsor of 'circular roots'.
ideas.modern_name: Torsor comparison / rigidification data (a μ_2-torsor trivialized via μ_4^*)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard torsor bookkeeping; no specific attribution

ideas.what: Parametrizing linear isomorphisms of lines into a μ_2-twisted line F(ω) by families of elements of F indexed by ω and homogeneous of degree −1, subject to an equivariance condition.
ideas.modern_name: Twisting by a μ_2-torsor; homogeneous functions as sections of the dual line

ideas.what: Intrinsic description of Legendre normal-form data attached to a 4-element set J and the conic Σ ⊂ P(Ker(k^J → k)).
ideas.modern_name: Legendre level structure / Γ(2)-structures and the λ-line, described coordinate-free
ideas.usually_credited_to: Legendre form classical; moduli with level 2 over Z[1/2]: Igusa, Deligne–Rapoport, Katz–Mazur

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine linear-algebra bookkeeping inside a larger, unpublished intrinsic treatment of Legendre structures. The page itself contains no new result or connection; only the overall program (coordinate-free Legendre pinnings via 4-point sets) is mildly interesting, and it is not specific to this page.
transcription_corrections: 'α = α_{[-K-]}' should read α = α_κ (kappa, the pinning), and 'K', 'Ǩ_i' throughout are κ, κ̌_i.
Margin NB is better read as: 'NB Condition: donnée d'un iso α : μ_4^* ≃ ω; dans [ce cas] les deux relations (67) [sont] équivalentes'.
The line before (71) is 'ψ^{ω'}(δ) = −(1/i) ψ^ω(δ)' with an underbrace showing −1/i = i.
'(+donnant un préalable α+)' is likely 'donnant au préalable α' (α given beforehand).
